maria: Heads-up — saw a p99 latency spike on canary after the fused-paged-attn merge. p50 ~ 6ms (same), p95 +12%, p99 +40%. Looks correlated with requests that hit our bf16 quantized KV cache layout.

ashok: Can you paste the selector logs + a quick profile snippet? wondering if kernel selection is doing the wrong fallback.

maria: selector log excerpt: 
```
2026-02-12T10:12:01Z selecting kernel: model=rr-small dtype=bf16 seq=1024 layout=interleaved_stride=24
2026-02-12T10:12:01Z chosen: fused_paged_attn (fastpath)
2026-02-12T10:12:01Z exec_time_ms=0.86  (expected 0.8)

2026-02-12T10:12:01Z selecting kernel: model=rr-small dtype=bf16 seq=1024 layout=interleaved_stride=24
2026-02-12T10:12:01Z chosen: fused_paged_attn (fastpath)
2026-02-12T10:12:01Z exec_time_ms=1.34  (much slower for some requests)
```
Posting a small nvprof-like sample: 
```
Kernel: fused_paged_attn  avg 0.9ms  p99 1.5ms  (1.5% hardware l2 miss)
Kernel: flash_hybrid_attn avg 1.1ms p99 1.2ms  (0.2% l2 miss)
```
Notably, when l2 miss spikes, fused_paged p99 goes way up.

jordan: Fused-paged assumes aligned per-key rows for vectorized ld/sto. If your stride is 24 bytes (interleaved with padding removed), you get unaligned 8/16-byte loads across warps — that can force the kernel into slower scalar paths or extra shuffles. What dtype is the model using at runtime? bf16 often packs weirdly with interleaving.

maria: We confirmed it's bf16. The KV layout is interleaved per-head to optimize cache for small seqs: memory layout = [K0h0..K0hN, K1h0..K1hN, ...] which created a 24B stride per key for N=3 heads-per-chunk. Diagram: 
```
addr: 0 -> K0h0 (16B)
addr:16 -> K0h1 (16B)
addr:32 -> K0h2 (16B)
addr:48 -> K1h0 (16B)  <-- but logical stride between K0 and K1 = 48 bytes
```
So loads from different tokens sometimes cross 64B cachelines in a non-warp-friendly way.

perf-bot: Regression alert: fused-paged-attn p99 increased by 38% in canary. Correlated with interleaved-layout batches. See ticket #INF-4823.

kevin: Two quick mitigations: (1) change kernel selector heuristics to prefer flash_hybrid when stride % 64 != 0 OR when dtype=bf16 and stride % 32 != 0 (empirically avoids scalar slowpaths), (2) add a layout-aware batch key so we don't mix interleaved and separate layouts in the same batch. Example change: 
```
batch_key = hash(model_id, dtype, layout_kind, stride_in_bytes)
```
Also propose to try the banked-separate layout that pads per-key rows to 64 bytes — bench command: 
```
./tools/bench_attn --model rr-small --layout=banked_padded --dtype=bf16 --seq=1024 --iters=500 --device A100
```
Run both A100 and H100 if possible.

sara: On batching heuristics: current batcher aggregates by model+dtype only, which lets mixed-layout requests be combined. That can flip kernel selection mid-batch (and the per-request kernel may still run but with suboptimal memory behavior). We should include layout hash in the batching key and add a cost penalty for batches that would force an unaligned fused path.

ashok: Also add a defensive check in fused_paged to detect unaligned effective stride and fall back early to flash_hybrid before starting heavy vector ops. Prefer that to subtle correctness/perf surprises.

maria: Agree. I'll run microbench for banked_padded vs current interleaved+pad on A100/H100 and post numbers & kernel traces. Rough plan: run kevin's bench then instrument with L2/L1 hit rates + per-warp stall counters.

jordan: FYI H100's cacheline/ldg semantics differ; H100 may tolerate some misalignment better but you'll still see variance with bf16. Good to test both.

kevin: If we confirm, I'll land two small changes: layout in batch key + selector fallback rule. Keep fused_paged as default for clean aligned layouts.

maria: ok will run benchmarks in the next 3 hours and update here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
